notes: D6-2: follow_up; the paper compares this previously identified hypervelocity star to the HeWD survivor tracks (T:p1-b7; T:p11-b3; I:p12-b3). US 708: follow_up; the paper's discovery statement places it with high-spatial-velocity objects and reports v≈900–1000 km/s, then compares it with the He-star tracks (T:p1-b7; T:p2-b0; T:p11-b5; I:p12-b3). J1332-3541 (plotted as J1332): follow_up; the paper identifies it as one of four newly discovered hypervelocity stars and shows it on the HR diagram (T:p11-b5; T:p12-b3; I:p12-b3). GD 492 (LP 40-365) was not rostered: the text only calls its class 'runaway objects' with 'mostly' 600–700 km/s ejection velocities and gives no explicit Galactic-unbound classification for it (T:p11-b6); the later 'GD 462' is treated as a typo for GD 492, supported by the earlier name and the GD492 label in I:p12-b3. The seven Gaia hypervelocity WDs are not individually named in the supplied text, so no separate star entries could be made.

D6-2: The paper mentions D6-2 only in comparison contexts. It reports T_eff = 7500 ± 100 K and R = 0.20 ± 0.01 R_sun (Chandra et al. 2022), a kinematic age of ≈10^5 yrs, and a photometric period of 15.4 hrs (T:p11-b3, T:p12-b2). None of these correspond to the target quantities. The paper does not report right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motions, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probabilities for D6-2.

US 708: The paper reports a "spatial velocity" for US 708 without explicitly stating the reference frame (T:p1-b7; T:p2-b0). Assigning these values to galactic_rest_frame_velocity treats "spatial velocity" as the total three-dimensional space velocity; this frame interpretation should be treated with caution. Other US 708 values in the paper (T_eff = 47200 K, log g = 5.69, adopted mass 0.3 M_sun, and disk-crossing time ~10^7 yr) are not among the requested quantities.

J1332-3541: The target J1332-3541 (J1332) appears in this paper only as a comparison hypervelocity star. The only reported properties are a temperature of 70,000 K and an uncertain radius R = 0.017_{-0.007}^{+0.013} R_sun "due to its uncertain distance" (T:p11-b5), plus an illustrative position in the HR diagram (Figure 8, I:p12-b3). No right ascension, declination, distance value, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for J1332, so none of the listable quantities can be extracted.
